_note: Family curation. `merges` folds vault instance_of targets that have no note into an existing family. `families.<slug>` may override name, oneLine, body (plain site prose, never Jung's words), spectrum.position, palette. `definitionPick` selects verbatim records from the vault data/mentions.jsonl (vol + para + quote prefix) for a family definition — the quote is never typed here; a pick that does not match verbatim is omitted loudly by the ingest.

anima-figure.name: Anima figure
anima-figure.oneLine: The woman behind a man's moods and projections: muse, siren, unknown guide.

anima-mundi.name: Anima mundi
anima-mundi.oneLine: The world-soul pictured as a guiding woman between God and nature.

anthropos.name: Anthropos
anthropos.oneLine: The primordial cosmic man in whom the divine world-principle appears.

antichrist.name: Antichrist
antichrist.oneLine: The adversary who follows Christ as a shadow follows the body.

ape.name: Ape
ape.oneLine: The divine, archaic and diabolical ape: instinct that mimics the spirit.

arrow.name: Arrow
arrow.oneLine: The wound shot from outside that proves to come from within.

ascent-descent.name: Ascent and descent
ascent-descent.oneLine: The work as a cycle: spirit rises to fetch the seed, then falls to fertilize the earth.

ass.name: Ass
ass.oneLine: The ass as bearer of mana: humble beast, sacred burden.

atman-brahman.name: Atman and Brahman
atman-brahman.oneLine: The Upanishadic self as light and cosmic ground; the golden germ.

bird.name: Bird
bird.oneLine: Winged carriers of spirit and thought, messengers between worlds.

cave.name: Cave
cave.oneLine: The dark enclosure of birth, initiation and rebirth, where the hidden is kept.

chakra.name: Chakra
chakra.oneLine: The yogic body-map of wheel and lotus centres, climbing from root to crown.

chalice.name: Chalice
chalice.oneLine: The vessel that heals, sanctifies and divines; the hollowed horn.

christ-figure.name: Christ figure
christ-figure.oneLine: Christ as ideal, mediator and shepherd: the figure of wholeness in the Christian world.

churinga.name: Churinga
churinga.oneLine: Decorated sacred stones of Central Australian tribes, bearers of ancestral soul.

definitionPick.starts: The churinga of the Australian aborigines is a similar energ

circle.name: Circle
circle.oneLine: The closed round form: wholeness without beginning or end.

circulation-of-light.name: Circulation of light
circulation-of-light.oneLine: Rotation about a centre as the movement of the psyche and of light.

coniunctio.name: Coniunctio
coniunctio.oneLine: The union of opposites: king and queen, sun and moon, conscious and unconscious.

corn-god.name: Corn god
corn-god.oneLine: The god who is food: the grain buried, sprouting and eaten.

cross.name: Cross
cross.oneLine: Four directions met at a centre: instrument of suffering and sign of the quaternity.

crown.name: Crown
crown.oneLine: The circle of rule and radiance set on the head of the transformed.

demiurge.name: Demiurge
demiurge.oneLine: The ignorant or flawed maker-god of the Gnostic cosmos.

devil.name: Devil
devil.oneLine: The adversary as intellect: Mephisto, the shadow side of the sacred.

dismemberment.name: Dismemberment
dismemberment.oneLine: The god torn apart and scattered so that he can be gathered anew.

divine-child.name: Divine child
divine-child.oneLine: The newborn god, threatened at birth and strangely invincible.

divine-pair.name: Divine pair
divine-pair.oneLine: God and goddess as one paired form: majestic father and majestic mother.

dog.name: Dog
dog.oneLine: Loyal companion and guardian of the threshold, hound of the underworld.

double.name: Double
double.oneLine: The paired mortal and immortal twin: the Dioscuri, the second bird in the tree.

dove.name: Dove
dove.oneLine: The white bird of the whitening: the pneuma that descends and purifies.

dragon.name: Dragon
dragon.oneLine: The chaos-monster set against the highest god, and the hero's first adversary.

dual-mother.name: Dual mother
dual-mother.oneLine: Being born of two mothers, one human and one divine.

eagle.name: Eagle
eagle.oneLine: The bird of spirit and sun, the high counterpart of the serpent.

eye.name: Eye
eye.oneLine: The eye as seeing and as womb: the little image in the pupil.

filius-philosophorum.name: Filius philosophorum
filius-philosophorum.oneLine: The alchemists' son: a hermaphroditic child born of the prima materia.

fire.name: Fire
fire.oneLine: The fire of the work: Mercurius as the only fire; fire as dynamism, passion and emotion.

fish.name: Fish
fish.oneLine: Redeemer, soul and food: Oannes, Ichthys, the double fish of the zodiac.

furnace.name: Furnace
furnace.oneLine: The athanor, the fiery kiln where the matter is tried and changed.

garden.name: Garden
garden.oneLine: The walled green space of the work: paradise recovered, where the sun rises.

giant.name: Giant
giant.oneLine: The oversized primordial being: ogre, titan, threat to the child-hero.

god-image.name: God image
god-image.oneLine: The inherited set of images in which the divine is pictured.

golden-flower.name: Golden flower
golden-flower.oneLine: The solar essence blooming as a flower: Chinese golden flower, Western rose.

grail.name: Grail
grail.oneLine: The shining vessel and castle at the end of the quest.

head.name: Head
head.oneLine: The head as seat of mind and omega element: the sons of the Golden Head.

heart.name: Heart
heart.oneLine: The bodily centre and the deep heart of the mystics.

helen-of-troy.name: Helen of Troy
helen-of-troy.oneLine: The ever-returning beauty: cause of war, companion of Simon Magus, Faust's Helen.

hermaphrodite.name: Hermaphrodite
hermaphrodite.oneLine: Primal bisexual wholeness: Plato's original man, the alchemical double being.

holy-ghost.name: Holy Ghost
holy-ghost.oneLine: The third person of the Trinity, descending into matter in alchemical thought.

homunculus.name: Homunculus
homunculus.oneLine: The little man of the alchemists, formed in the vessel.

horn.name: Horn
horn.oneLine: The single pointed outgrowth that heals: unicorn, rhinoceros, antelope.

horse.name: Horse
horse.oneLine: The spirit-animal that talks and knows: the unconscious as swift, miraculous beast.

i-ching-hexagram.name: I Ching hexagram
i-ching-hexagram.oneLine: The line-figures of the I Ching, from the river-map of the dragon's magic signs.

island.name: Island
island.oneLine: The enclosed land in the sea: castle-rock and paradise as refuge.

khidr.name: Khidr
khidr.oneLine: The ever-living guide of Islamic tradition who teaches at the meeting of the seas.

king-queen-pair.name: King and queen
king-queen-pair.oneLine: The royal pair of the work: sun and moon, brother and sister in the bath.

lamb.name: Lamb
lamb.oneLine: The sacrificial white animal and its Christian sublimation, the Lamb of God.

lamia.name: Lamia
lamia.oneLine: The woman-monster who takes children and lovers.

lapis.name: Lapis
lapis.oneLine: The stone that is no stone: end of the work, body, spirit and medicine at once.

lingam-yoni.name: Lingam and yoni
lingam-yoni.oneLine: Union as image: the standing stone in its base, Shiva and Shakti.

lion.name: Lion
lion.oneLine: The royal, devouring beast of the alchemists: Mercurius in his volatile form.

lion-headed-god.name: Lion-headed god
lion-headed-god.oneLine: The leontocephalic figure of unending time: Mithraic Aion, the lion-faced demiurge.

lotus.name: Lotus
lotus.oneLine: The seated flower in which gods are born and enthroned.

lumen-naturae.name: Lumen naturae
lumen-naturae.oneLine: The innate light of nature, a second source of knowledge beside revelation.

magical-companion.name: Magical companion
magical-companion.oneLine: The unrecognized fellow-traveller who joins the quester on the road.

magician.name: Magician
magician.oneLine: The old master of dream and fairytale, in white and in black.

magnet.name: Magnet
magnet.oneLine: The attractive stone: an invisible pull toward the centre.

maiden.name: Maiden
maiden.oneLine: The young woman of dream and myth: helper, bride, bait, soul in bloom.

mandala.name: Mandala
mandala.oneLine: Circles and centred quaternary figures that arise spontaneously: pictures of wholeness.

melusina.name: Melusina
melusina.oneLine: The half-woman, half-serpent water-spirit of Lusignan.

mercurius.name: Mercurius
mercurius.oneLine: The double-natured spirit of quicksilver: thief's god, guide and trickster.

merkabah.name: Merkabah
merkabah.oneLine: Ezekiel's throne-chariot: four living creatures, four wheels, the glory enthroned.

monster.name: Monster
monster.oneLine: The many-membered composite beast of the prima materia.

moon.name: Moon
moon.oneLine: The night light that holds the dead and the seed.

moth.name: Moth
moth.oneLine: The soul-creature drawn fatally to the flame.

mother-goddess.name: Mother goddess
mother-goddess.oneLine: Goddess, Mother of God, Virgin, Sophia: the many figures of the mother.

mothers-of-faust.name: Mothers of Faust
mothers-of-faust.oneLine: The formless, generative realm of the Mothers, reached by a key in Faust II.

mountain.name: Mountain
mountain.oneLine: The high place of ascent and vision, the axis of the world.

night-sea-journey.name: Night sea journey
night-sea-journey.oneLine: The hero's descent into the monster's belly and the deep, to rise renewed.

nigredo.name: Nigredo
nigredo.oneLine: The blackening: the initial state of the work (CW12 ¶334).
body: Jung writes that the nigredo is present from the beginning as a quality of the prima materia or produced by the separation of the elements (CW12 ¶334). He writes that the nigredo corresponds to the encounter with the shadow (CW12 ¶41).

nixie.name: Nixie
nixie.oneLine: The half-fish water-maiden of the fisherman's net: siren, nymph, lamia.

paradise.name: Paradise
paradise.oneLine: The enclosed garden of origin and end, with the tree of life.

peacock.name: Peacock
peacock.oneLine: The spread tail of all colours, seen just before the whitening.

pearl.name: Pearl
pearl.oneLine: The treasure at the bottom of the water, guarded by the dragon.

phallus.name: Phallus
phallus.oneLine: The ithyphallic old man and the generative power: Hermes Kyllenios.

philosophers-egg.name: Philosophers' egg
philosophers-egg.oneLine: The sealed vessel as egg: the germ of the stone.

phoenix.name: Phoenix
phoenix.oneLine: The fire-bird that renews itself from its own ashes.

planetary-gods.name: Planetary gods
planetary-gods.oneLine: The seven planetary deities of ascent-rites, of Hades and of the metals.

plough.name: Plough
plough.oneLine: The tool that makes the earth fruitful, echoing the marriage act.

point.name: Point
point.oneLine: The dimensionless centre from which the circle is drawn.

prima-materia.name: Prima materia
prima-materia.oneLine: The initial stuff of the work: dragon, tail-eater, dark chaos.

quaternity.name: Quaternity
quaternity.oneLine: Four-ness of the whole: four functions round a centre, four gates, four evangelists.

raven.name: Raven
raven.oneLine: The black bird of the blackening, messenger of the dark stage of the work.

rebis.name: Rebis
rebis.oneLine: The two-bodied child of the coniunctio, half male and half female.

resurrection.name: Resurrection
resurrection.oneLine: The dead awakened: the king reborn from the dungeon.

rose.name: Rose
rose.oneLine: The rose as mandala-centre and the philosophers' rose garden.

rotundum.name: Rotundum
rotundum.oneLine: The round thing of alchemy, the perfect sphere of the work.

rubedo.name: Rubedo
rubedo.oneLine: The reddening: the marriage of Sol and Luna (CW14 ¶307).
body: Jung writes that the alchemists termed the stage in which the marriage of the red man and the white woman is consummated the rubedo (CW14 ¶307). He writes that the rubedo is the second and usually final stage (CW14 ¶434).

sacrifice.name: Sacrifice
sacrifice.oneLine: The act of transformation in which priest and victim are one.

salamander.name: Salamander
salamander.oneLine: The fire-dwelling lizard that lives in the flame and is not consumed.

salt.name: Salt
salt.oneLine: Salt as arcane substance: a cosmic, lunar and feminine principle in alchemy.

scarab.name: Scarab
scarab.oneLine: The dung-beetle as emblem of self-generation, pushing its ball from the earth.

senex-figure.name: Senex
senex-figure.oneLine: The old man of dream and myth: guide, teacher, bearer of meaning.

serpent.name: Serpent
serpent.oneLine: Circle-maker, earth-power, mercurial spirit: the snake in its many valences.

shiva.name: Shiva
shiva.oneLine: The Indian god with his Shakti: the Tantric pair in continuous union.

sol-niger.name: Sol niger
sol-niger.oneLine: The blackened sun: the centre darkened at the start of the work.

solificatio.name: Solificatio
solificatio.oneLine: Becoming sun: the crowned initiate, the face that shines like the sun.

sophia.name: Sophia
sophia.oneLine: Divine Wisdom personified as feminine, bride and teacher of the art.

soul-bird.name: Soul bird
soul-bird.oneLine: The soul as a small bird, led out of the grave by the guide of souls.

spark.name: Spark
spark.oneLine: The scintilla: a small light hidden in the dark of matter.

stag.name: Stag
stag.oneLine: The fleeing, uncatchable deer of the alchemists, paired with the unicorn.

star.name: Star
star.oneLine: Rays from a centre: pentagram, many-rayed star, star-cross.

stone.name: Stone
stone.oneLine: The stone that kills and quickens, found on the dunghill and crowned as king.

sulphur.name: Sulphur
sulphur.oneLine: Sulphur, the fiery active principle of the metals in alchemy.

sun.name: Sun
sun.oneLine: Source of life and wholeness: Helios, the shining face, the red ball, the gold.

sun-hero.name: Sun hero
sun-hero.oneLine: The solar hero who is swallowed and born again with each day.

swan.name: Swan
swan.oneLine: The white water-bird of the soul, between earth and sky.

swastika.name: Swastika
swastika.oneLine: The gamma-cross in right- and left-hand rotation, alone and inside mandalas.

tao.name: Tao
tao.oneLine: The Way: the central light between the eyes, the unity of life and consciousness.

tauroctony.name: Tauroctony
tauroctony.oneLine: The Mithraic scene of the god kneeling on the bull, sword at its shoulder.

temenos.name: Temenos
temenos.oneLine: The delimited sacred space: snake-circle, city wall, church precinct, cloister garden.

tetramorph.name: Tetramorph
tetramorph.oneLine: The four creatures of man, lion, ox and eagle about the throne.

toad.name: Toad
toad.oneLine: The chthonic, devouring creature of damp and dark.

treasure.name: Treasure
treasure.oneLine: The precious thing guarded in the dark by snake or dragon.

tree.name: Tree
tree.oneLine: The Tree of Life and the Tree of the Sefiroth, in Crowley, Jung and von Franz.

trickster-figure.name: Trickster figure
trickster-figure.oneLine: The shape-shifting fool of myth: culture-bringer, blunderer and scapegoat.

trinity.name: Trinity
trinity.oneLine: Three in one: the stone trinus et unus, king, son and spirit.

unicorn.name: Unicorn
unicorn.oneLine: The wild, chaste horned beast, where Christ and Mercurius meet in one image.

uroboros.name: Uroboros
uroboros.oneLine: The serpent or dragon devouring its own tail, closing the circle.

venus.name: Venus
venus.oneLine: Queen Venus: heavenly beauty set against terrible Proserpina.

vessel.name: Vessel
vessel.oneLine: The sealed glass vessel of the work: retort, pelican, womb.

virgin.name: Virgin
virgin.oneLine: The feminine carrier of the work in its virginal aspect: Mary, virgo terrae.

water.name: Water
water.oneLine: Water in the work: the aqua permanens, the living water, and the unconscious.

well-spring.name: Well and spring
well-spring.oneLine: The life-water and its source: fountain, spring, aqua nostra.

wind.name: Wind
wind.oneLine: The fertilizing breath: the West Wind, father of the winds, spirit that conceives.

world-clock.name: World clock
world-clock.oneLine: A clock-like mandala with a dark centre and turning rings.

world-wheel.name: World wheel
world-wheel.oneLine: The wheel of existence with the cock, snake and pig at its hub.

worm.name: Worm
worm.oneLine: The lowest, first form of renewal, from which the phoenix rises.

yantra.name: Yantra
yantra.oneLine: Geometric instrument of ritual: triangles, lotuses and circles round a point.

hero.name: Hero
hero.oneLine: The overcoming young hero: Jung’s Siegfried dream, and every young champion after.

death.name: Death
death.oneLine: The dying that turns into its opposite — the enantiodromia wheel.

greening-tree.name: Greening tree
greening-tree.oneLine: The greening man growing from the temple’s ruins — nature overtaking the ideal.

number.name: Number
number.oneLine: Number in Jung: an archetype of order that has become conscious, valid in both worlds.
body: Jung defines number psychologically as an archetype of order which has become conscious (CW8 ¶870, 1952), and writes that whole numbers are likewise archetypes of order (CW10 ¶805, 1958). He calls Number the great mediator, whose reality is valid in both worlds (CW10 ¶778). The instances here are dreams in which a number appears.
The six number archetypes, one to six, are tied to this family, and each has its own page.

air.name: Air
air.oneLine: One of the four elements: the volatile element rising from earth; also pneuma.
body: An alchemical author, quoted in CW12 ¶397, calls air uncommonly light and invisible, but inside heavy, visible and solid.
Jung writes that pneuma, like spirit, originally meant air in motion (CW14 ¶161).

earth-element.name: Earth
earth-element.oneLine: The fourth or fifth element: the black basis of the work, not its goal.
body: Jung writes that earth occupies the central position as the fifth element, though it is not the quintessence and goal of the work but its basis (CW14 ¶249), and that in the Axiom of Maria earth represents the fourth (CW14 ¶656).
Jung writes of the nigredo as terra nigra (CW14 ¶264).

ether.name: Ether
ether.oneLine: Aether: the quintessence in alchemy, the primordial breath, and the physicist's ether.
body: CW12 ¶371 states that ether is the quintessence; Jung writes that aether, the primordial breath or soul-substance, is a concept found all over the world (CW7 ¶151).
Pauli writes that through the postulate of relativity ether as a substance has been removed from physical theories (pdf p18).

feeling.name: Feeling
feeling.oneLine: The function of valuation: a content is accepted or rejected, liked or disliked.
body: Jung writes that feeling is primarily a process between the ego and a given content that imparts to the content a value of acceptance or rejection (CW6 ¶724).
He calls feeling a kind of judgment whose aim is a subjective criterion of acceptance or rejection (CW6 ¶725), and undirected feeling feeling-intuition (CW6 ¶729).

intuition.name: Intuition
intuition.oneLine: The function that mediates perceptions in an unconscious way.
body: Jung calls intuition an irrational function of perception whose contents have the character of being given (CW6 ¶770).
It stands in a compensatory relationship to sensation, and is with it the matrix out of which thinking and feeling develop as rational functions (CW6 ¶772).

quintessence.name: Quintessence
quintessence.oneLine: The quinta essentia: the Philosophers' Stone, and the unity of the four elements.
body: Jung writes that the quinta essentia is identical with the Philosophers' Stone (CW10 ¶738), and speaks of the quintessential star, symbol of the unity of the four hostile elements (CW16 ¶403).
Von Franz writes that it is not merely a fifth element added on to the four, but represents their realized unity of existence (pdf p77).

sensation.name: Sensation
sensation.oneLine: The function that establishes that something is, through the senses and the body.
body: Jung writes that sensation is the psychological function that mediates the perception of a physical stimulus, primarily sense perception (CW6 ¶792, ¶793).
Sensation tells that something is, and does not tell what it is (CW18 ¶21).

spiritus.name: Spiritus
spiritus.oneLine: Air in motion: spiritus and pneuma, and the volatile side of Mercurius.
body: Jung writes that the texts often use pneuma and spiritus in the original concrete sense of air in motion (CW13 pdf p244).
The spiritus mercurialis is the alchemists' guide (CW12 ¶84); Mercurius in his volatile form of spiritus is a parallel of the Holy Ghost (CW12 ¶518).

thinking.name: Thinking
thinking.oneLine: The function that links ideas by means of a concept: an act of judgment.
body: Jung writes that the term thinking should be confined to the linking up of ideas by means of a concept, in other words to an act of judgment (CW6 ¶831).
Directed thinking is a rational function, and undirected thinking an irrational one (CW6 ¶832).

kether.name: Kether
kether.oneLine: The Crown, the first of the ten: Crowley's number 1 and Jung's upward-growing root.
body: Crowley gives Kether the number 1 (pdf p33) and writes that from Kether, the supreme, influence descends directly (pdf p211).
Jung writes that Kether, the Crown, corresponds to the upward-growing root of the Tree of the Sefiroth (CW14 ¶18).

chokmah.name: Chokmah
chokmah.oneLine: Wisdom, the Logos: Crowley's number 2, which he calls the first manifestation.
body: Crowley writes that the 2 pertains to Chokmah (pdf p35), and that the magical manifestation of Chokmah is Wisdom, the Logos (pdf p211).
He names the Father, who is Wisdom, as the highest form of Mercury (pdf p79), and writes Mercury as Chokmah, through whom alone we can approach Kether (pdf p121).

binah.name: Binah
binah.oneLine: Understanding, the Great Mother: Crowley's number 3, with Saturn and the Moon.
body: Crowley writes that Binah, the Great Sea, is the Moon in one aspect, but Saturn in another (pdf p199), and that Saturn appears in Binah in respect of its blackness (pdf p110).
Jung writes that in Binah is rooted the tree of life (CW13 ¶411).

chesed.name: Chesed
chesed.oneLine: Crowley's number 4, with Jupiter and Water; Jung's kesed, love, a side of the Tree.
body: Crowley attributes the Four cards to Chesed (pdf p176) and writes that Chesed is attributed to Jupiter, who is the Demiurge (pdf p176).
Jung writes that kesed (love) and din (justice) are the two sides of the cabalistic Tree of the Sephiroth (CW9ii ¶105).

geburah.name: Geburah
geburah.oneLine: Crowley's number 5: the Five cards are referred to Geburah.
body: Crowley refers the Fives to the Sephira Geburah because it is a Five (pdf p40), and writes of Geburah of the suit of Fire (pdf p189) and of the suit of Earth (pdf p231).
Of the Five of Cups he writes that Mars is the manifestation on the lowest plane of Geburah (pdf p202).

tiphareth.name: Tiphareth
tiphareth.oneLine: Crowley's number 6, the centre: the Sun in the planets, the Son in Tetragrammaton.
body: Crowley attributes the Sixes to Tiphareth (pdf p177) and calls the number Six the centre of the system (pdf p21); in the planetary system it represents the Sun, and in the system of Tetragrammaton the Son (pdf p177).
Jung writes that Tifereth occupies the middle position of the Sefiroth system (CW14 ¶592) and is named the sun (CW14 ¶638).

netzach.name: Netzach
netzach.oneLine: Crowley's number 7, the Sephira of Venus, which he says means victory.
body: Crowley attributes the Sevens to Netzach (pdf p178) and calls Netzach the Sephira of Venus, which means victory (pdf p219).
Jung writes that Yesod unites the emanation of the right, masculine side, Nezach, life-force, with the left, feminine side, Hod (CW14 ¶635).

hod.name: Hod
hod.oneLine: Crowley's number 8, airy and mercurial; Jung's Hod, beauty, on the left of the Tree.
body: Crowley attributes the four Eights to Hod (pdf p179), writes that the number Eight, Hod, represents Mercury (pdf p234), and calls Hod, in his system, Airy and Mercurial (pdf p263).
Jung writes that Yesod unites Nezach on the right with Hod, beauty, on the left (CW14 ¶635).

yesod.name: Yesod
yesod.oneLine: Crowley's number 9 and the Moon: the foundation of the Tree, in Jung the ninth Sefira.
body: Crowley attributes the Nines to Yesod (pdf p180) and writes of the moon of Yesod, the foundation of the Tree (pdf p110).
Jung writes that Jezoth, Yesod, is the ninth and middle Sefira in the lowest triad of the Cabalistic tree (CW14 ¶634), and that it unites Nezach on the right with Hod on the left (CW14 ¶635).

malkuth.name: Malkuth
malkuth.oneLine: Crowley's number 10 and Earth, right down in Assiah, depending on the other nine.
body: Crowley attributes the Tens to Malkuth (pdf p181) and writes that the number Ten refers to Malkuth, which depends from the other nine Sephiroth (pdf p195); the tenth Sephira refers to Earth (pdf p266).
Jung writes that Malchuth is the underlying feminine principle (CW14 ¶18).

citrinitas.name: Citrinitas
citrinitas.oneLine: Jung lists xanthosis, the yellowing, third of the four stages (CW12 ¶333).
body: Jung gives the four stages as melanosis, leukosis, xanthosis and iosis, after the colours mentioned in Heraclitus (CW12 ¶333). He writes that the transition to the rubedo is formed by the citrinitas (CW12 ¶334).

aries.name: Aries
aries.oneLine: Burt's Aries: the Age of the Ram, Mars and the Hero; the search for a separate identity.
body: Burt's chapter on Aries is titled The Search for a Separate Identity (pdf p23).
Burt writes that the Age of Aries is the Age of the Ram, of Mars and of the Hero (pdf p23), and that Aries is outward drive and Logos (pdf p25).

taurus.name: Taurus
taurus.oneLine: Burt's Taurus: Fixed Earth, the bull and the goddess; the search for value and meaning.
body: Burt's chapter on Taurus is titled The Search for Value and Meaning (pdf p59).
Burt gives the bull, the goddess and the Buddha as symbols for the Age of Taurus, and Venus/Aphrodite as mundane ruler and Vulcan/Hephaestus as esoteric ruler (pdf p59).

gemini.name: Gemini
gemini.oneLine: Burt's Gemini: Mutable Air, ruled by Mercury/Hermes; the search for variety.
body: Burt's chapter on Gemini is titled The Search for Variety (pdf p95).
Burt calls Gemini Mutable Air, which represents observation, analysis, rational classification of data and objectivity (pdf p98), and the most versatile archetype (pdf p115).

cancer.name: Cancer
cancer.oneLine: Burt's Cancer: the Cosmic Womb, the first Water sign; the search for the Mother Goddess.
body: Burt's chapter on Cancer is titled The Search for the Mother Goddess (pdf p135).
Burt calls Cancer the Cosmic Womb and the first Water sign (pdf p135), and names the Moon as Cancer's ruler, the Giver of Form (pdf p136).

leo.name: Leo
leo.oneLine: Burt's Leo: the solar, Masculine principle; the search for being and wholeness.
body: Burt's chapter on Leo is titled The Search for Being and Wholeness (pdf p175).
Burt writes that in Leo we arrive at the solar, or Masculine principle (pdf p175), with the sun as mundane and esoteric ruler (pdf p178).

virgo.name: Virgo
virgo.oneLine: Burt's Virgo: an Earth sign ruled by Hermes; the search for meaningful service.
body: Burt's chapter on Virgo is titled The Search for Meaningful Service (pdf p211).
Burt writes that Hermes rules the Earth sign Virgo (pdf p211) and that its esoteric ruler is the Moon (pdf p236).

libra.name: Libra
libra.oneLine: Burt's Libra: the seventh sign, the second Air sign; the search for the soul mate.
body: Burt's chapter on Libra is titled The Search for the Soul Mate (pdf p253).
Burt calls Libra the seventh sign, the second Air sign and the third Cardinal sign (pdf p253), and writes of Aphrodite, Goddess of Love, aesthetics and civilized good taste (pdf p253).

scorpio.name: Scorpio
scorpio.oneLine: Burt's Scorpio: mundane rulers Mars and Pluto; the search for the transformation.
body: Burt's chapter on Scorpio is titled The Search for the Transformation (pdf p295).
Burt names Mars and Pluto as the mundane rulers of Scorpio (pdf p295), and writes that Scorpio's work is to transform, to change and refine the form (pdf p301).

sagittarius.name: Sagittarius
sagittarius.oneLine: Burt's Sagittarius: a solar Fire sign, ruled by Zeus or Jupiter; the search for wisdom.
body: Burt's chapter on Sagittarius is titled The Search for Wisdom (pdf p339).
Burt writes that Zeus, or Jupiter, is the ruler of Sagittarius (pdf p339), and that astrologers have associated the sign with Spirit and expansion of awareness (pdf p339).

capricorn.name: Capricorn
capricorn.oneLine: Burt's Capricorn: time, Chronus or Saturn; the search for dharma.
body: Burt's chapter on Capricorn is titled The Search for Dharma (pdf p379).
Burt writes that the Capricorn archetype includes every concept, sense and meaning of time (pdf p381), and describes Chronus, or Saturn, as Father Time (pdf p379).

aquarius.name: Aquarius
aquarius.oneLine: Burt's Aquarius: the last Fixed sign, an Air sign; the search for the Holy Grail.
body: Burt's chapter on Aquarius is titled The Search for the Holy Grail (pdf p447).
Burt calls Aquarius the last of the four Fixed signs and an Air sign with a mental approach to life (pdf p447), and links it to the question central to the Grail Quest (pdf p450).

pisces.name: Pisces
pisces.oneLine: Burt's Pisces: Mutable Water, the cosmic ocean; the search for the castle of peace.
body: Burt's chapter on Pisces is titled The Search for the Castle of Peace (pdf p509).
Burt calls Pisces the last of the four Mutable signs, Mutable Water (pdf p509), and the cosmic ocean of infinity (pdf p509).

thoth-tarot.name: The Thoth Tarot
thoth-tarot.oneLine: Crowley's Tarot: a pictorial representation of the Forces of Nature (pdf p29).
body: Crowley calls the Tarot a pictorial representation of the Forces of Nature (pdf p29) and an admirable symbolic picture of the Universe, based on the data of the Holy Qabalah (pdf p13).

thoth-major-arcana.name: The Major Arcana
thoth-major-arcana.oneLine: Crowley's twenty-two Trumps, referred to the twenty-two Paths of the Tree of Life.
body: Crowley says the twenty-two Trumps refer to the twenty-two Paths (pdf p261), and that one letter of the Hebrew alphabet goes to each path (pdf p36).

thoth-minor-arcana.name: The Minor Arcana
thoth-minor-arcana.oneLine: Crowley's small cards: forty, numbered one to ten, in four suits by the four elements.

thoth-wands.name: Wands
thoth-wands.oneLine: Crowley's Wands: Fire (pdf p24) and Aries (pdf p35); the flames of the Ace are Yods.
body: Crowley says Wands has the attribution of Aries, and represents swift violence of onset, the lightning flash (pdf p35). He says the flames of the Ace of Wands are Yods, arranged in the form of the Tree of Life (pdf p183).

thoth-cups.name: Cups
thoth-cups.oneLine: Crowley's Cups: Water (pdf p24); the Ace is the essential form of the Holy Grail.
body: Crowley calls the Ace of Cups the feminine complement of the Ace of Wands, derived from the Yoni and the Moon (pdf p196). He says that upon the dark sea of Binah, the Great Mother, are Lotuses (pdf p196).

thoth-swords.name: Swords
thoth-swords.oneLine: Crowley's Swords: Air (pdf p24); the Ace is the Essence of the Vau of Tetragrammaton.
body: Crowley says Air is the result of the conjunction of Fire and Water, and that in nature the obvious symbol of Air is the Wind (pdf p210). He says the Princes represent the Forces of the letter Vau in the Name (pdf p139).

thoth-disks.name: Disks
thoth-disks.oneLine: Crowley's Disks: Earth (pdf p24); the Disk is a whirling emblem, not a Coin (pdf p225).
body: Crowley says the Disks are no longer to be considered as Coins, and that the Disk is a whirling emblem (pdf p225). He writes that the Earthy component, Hé final, the Daughter, is set upon the Throne of the Mother (pdf p225).

thoth-knight-of-wands.name: Knight of Wands
thoth-knight-of-wands.oneLine: The fiery part of Fire, Yodh of the Name; span Scorpio to Sagittarius (Crowley).

thoth-queen-of-wands.name: Queen of Wands
thoth-queen-of-wands.oneLine: The watery part of Fire, Hé of the Name; span Pisces to Aries (Crowley).

thoth-prince-of-wands.name: Prince of Wands
thoth-prince-of-wands.oneLine: The airy part of Fire, Vau of the Name; span Cancer to Leo (Crowley).

thoth-princess-of-wands.name: Princess of Wands
thoth-princess-of-wands.oneLine: The earthy part of Fire, final Hé of the Name; a quadrant about the North Pole (Crowley).

thoth-knight-of-cups.name: Knight of Cups
thoth-knight-of-cups.oneLine: The fiery part of Water, Yodh of the Name; span Aquarius to Pisces (Crowley).

thoth-queen-of-cups.name: Queen of Cups
thoth-queen-of-cups.oneLine: The watery part of Water, Hé of the Name; span Gemini to Cancer (Crowley).

thoth-prince-of-cups.name: Prince of Cups
thoth-prince-of-cups.oneLine: The airy part of Water, Vau of the Name; span Libra to Scorpio (Crowley).

thoth-princess-of-cups.name: Princess of Cups
thoth-princess-of-cups.oneLine: The earthy part of Water, final Hé of the Name; no zodiacal attribution (Crowley).

thoth-knight-of-swords.name: Knight of Swords
thoth-knight-of-swords.oneLine: The fiery part of Air, Yodh of the Name; span Taurus to Gemini (Crowley).

thoth-queen-of-swords.name: Queen of Swords
thoth-queen-of-swords.oneLine: The watery part of Air, Hé of the Name; span Virgo to Libra (Crowley).

thoth-prince-of-swords.name: Prince of Swords
thoth-prince-of-swords.oneLine: The airy part of Air, Vau of the Name; span Capricorn to Aquarius (Crowley).

thoth-princess-of-swords.name: Princess of Swords
thoth-princess-of-swords.oneLine: The earthy part of Air, final Hé of the Name; no zodiacal attribution (Crowley).

thoth-knight-of-disks.name: Knight of Disks
thoth-knight-of-disks.oneLine: The fiery part of Earth, Yodh of the Name; span Leo to Virgo (Crowley).

thoth-queen-of-disks.name: Queen of Disks
thoth-queen-of-disks.oneLine: The watery part of Earth, Hé of the Name; span Sagittarius to Capricorn (Crowley).

thoth-prince-of-disks.name: Prince of Disks
thoth-prince-of-disks.oneLine: The airy part of Earth, Vau of the Name; span Aries to Taurus (Crowley).

thoth-princess-of-disks.name: Princess of Disks
thoth-princess-of-disks.oneLine: The earthy part of Earth, final Hé of the Name; no zodiacal attribution (Crowley).

thoth-fool.name: Atu 0 · The Fool
thoth-fool.oneLine: Crowley's Atu 0: the negative above the Tree, attributed to Air and the letter Aleph.
body: Crowley says the number of the card should be 0, and that it represents the Negative above the Tree of Life, the source of all things (pdf p46). He attributes it to the letter Aleph, which means an Ox (pdf p46), and calls the path of Aleph the Path of the Pure Fool (pdf p116).

thoth-magus.name: Atu I · The Magus
thoth-magus.oneLine: Crowley's Atu I: Mercury and the letter Beth, the Logos by whom the worlds were made.
body: Crowley says the card is referred to the letter Beth, which means a house, and is attributed to the planet Mercury (pdf p58). He says it represents the Wisdom, the Will, the Word, the Logos by whom the worlds were created (pdf p58).

thoth-priestess.name: Atu II · The Priestess
thoth-priestess.oneLine: Crowley's Atu II: the Moon, the letter Gimel, the card joining number 1 to number 6.
body: Crowley says the card is referred to the letter Gimel, which means a Camel, and to the Moon (pdf p61). He describes it as the card joining the number 1 to the number 6 (pdf p27).

thoth-empress.name: Atu III · The Empress
thoth-empress.oneLine: Crowley's Atu III: Venus and the letter Daleth, the path that unites Chokmah with Binah.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Daleth, which means a door, and refers to the planet Venus (pdf p64). He says the doctrine implied is that the fundamental formula of the Universe is Love (pdf p64).

thoth-emperor.name: Atu IV · The Emperor
thoth-emperor.oneLine: Crowley's Atu IV: Aries under Mars, the letter Tzaddi, and authority derived from Chokmah.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Tzaddi and refers to the sign of Aries, ruled by Mars, in which the Sun is exalted (pdf p66). He says its authority is derived from Chokmah, the creative Wisdom, and is exerted upon Tiphareth, the organized man (pdf p67).

thoth-hierophant.name: Atu V · The Hierophant
thoth-hierophant.oneLine: Crowley's Atu V: Taurus, the letter Vau (a nail), and microcosm joined to macrocosm.
body: Crowley says the card is referred to the letter Vau, which means a Nail, and to Taurus (pdf p68). He gives its main reference as the uniting of the microcosm with the macrocosm (pdf p68), and calls it the aeon of Horus, of the Child (pdf p69).

thoth-lovers.name: Atu VI · The Lovers
thoth-lovers.oneLine: Crowley's Atu VI: Gemini under Mercury, the letter Zain (sword), from Binah to Tiphareth.
body: Crowley says Atu VI refers to Gemini, ruled by Mercury, and that the corresponding Hebrew letter is Zain, which means a Sword (pdf p70). He writes that Gemini leads from Binah to Tiphareth (pdf p72) and that the subject of the card is Analysis, followed by Synthesis (pdf p71).

thoth-chariot.name: Atu VII · The Chariot
thoth-chariot.oneLine: Crowley's Atu VII: Cancer, cardinal sign of Water, and the path from Binah to Geburah.
body: Crowley says Atu VII refers to the zodiacal sign of Cancer, the cardinal sign of the element of Water (pdf p74). He says Cancer represents the path which leads from the great Mother Binah to Geburah (pdf p74), and that the figure's only function is to bear the Holy Grail (pdf p75).

thoth-adjustment.name: Atu VIII · Adjustment
thoth-adjustment.oneLine: Crowley's Atu VIII, once Justice: Libra under Venus, and the exact justice of Nature.
body: Crowley says this card in the old pack was called Justice, and that it represents the sign of Libra, ruled by Venus, in which Saturn is exalted (pdf p76). He says the card is the feminine complement of the Fool, and that Nature is exact (pdf p76).

thoth-hermit.name: Atu IX · The Hermit
thoth-hermit.oneLine: Crowley's Atu IX: the letter Yod, the Hand, and Virgo, a sign ruled by Mercury.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Yod, which means the Hand (pdf p79), and to the sign of Virgo, ruled by Mercury, with Mercury exalted there (pdf p80). He says Yod symbolizes the Father, who is Wisdom (pdf p79).

thoth-fortune.name: Atu X · Fortune
thoth-fortune.oneLine: Crowley's Atu X: Jupiter, the Greater Fortune, the letter Kaph, and the change of state.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the planet Jupiter, the Greater Fortune in astrology (pdf p81). He says the card represents the Universe in its aspect as a continual change of state, and that Jupiter represents the element of luck (pdf p81).

thoth-lust.name: Atu XI · Lust
thoth-lust.oneLine: Crowley's Atu XI, Lust: the letter Teth (a serpent), the sign Leo, the Kerub of Fire.
body: Crowley says the Trump is assigned to the sign of Leo, and that the card is attributed to the letter Teth, which means a serpent (pdf p84). He writes that it is the Kerub of Fire, ruled by the Sun, and that it represents the act of the original marriage as it occurs in nature (pdf p84).

thoth-hanged-man.name: Atu XII · The Hanged Man
thoth-hanged-man.oneLine: Crowley's Hanged Man: the letter Mem and the element Water, a baptism that is a death.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Mem and represents the element of Water (pdf p87), and that Mem is one of the three great Mother Letters (pdf p89). He says it is a baptism and a death (pdf p87).

thoth-death.name: Atu XIII · Death
thoth-death.oneLine: Crowley's Death: a skeleton with a scythe, the letter Nun (a fish), Scorpio ruled by Mars.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Nun, which means a fish, and refers to the Zodiacal sign of Scorpio, which is ruled by Mars (pdf p90). He says the card represents the dance of death, the figure a skeleton bearing a scythe (pdf p91).

thoth-art.name: Atu XIV · Art
thoth-art.oneLine: Crowley's Art: the Arrow of directed Will, Sagittarius, the path from Yesod to Tiphareth.
body: Crowley says the card pertains to Sagittarius, the opposite to Gemini in the Zodiac, and that its path leads from the Moon of Yesod to the Sun of Tiphareth (pdf p92). He calls the Arrow the simplest and purest glyph of Mercury, being the symbol of directed Will (pdf p94).

thoth-devil.name: Atu XV · The Devil
thoth-devil.oneLine: Crowley's Devil: Pan the All-Begetter, the letter Ayin (an eye), Capricorn under Saturn.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Ayin, which means an Eye, and refers to Capricornus in the Zodiac (pdf p95). He says the sign is ruled by Saturn, who makes for selfhood and perpetuity, and that the card represents Pan Pangenetor, the All-Begetter (pdf p95).

thoth-tower.name: Atu XVI · The Tower
thoth-tower.oneLine: Crowley's Tower: the letter Pé (a mouth), Mars, destruction of existing material by fire.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Pé, which means a mouth, and refers to the planet Mars (pdf p98). He says the picture shows the destruction of existing material by fire, and that its dominating feature is the Eye of Horus (pdf p98, p99).

thoth-star.name: Atu XVII · The Star
thoth-star.oneLine: Crowley's Star: the letter He, the sign Aquarius, Nuith our Lady of the Stars.
body: Crowley says the card is attributed to the letter Hé and refers to the Zodiacal sign of Aquarius, the water-bearer (pdf p100). He says the picture represents Nuith, our Lady of the Stars (pdf p100), and that heaven itself is no more than a veil before the face of the immortal goddess (pdf p101).

thoth-moon.name: Atu XVIII · The Moon
thoth-moon.oneLine: Crowley's Moon: the letter Qoph, Pisces, her lowest avatar joining Netzach to Malkuth.
body: Crowley says the Eighteenth Trump is attributed to the letter Qoph, which represents Pisces in the Zodiac (pdf p103). He says that in this Trump, her lowest avatar, the Moon joins the earthy sphere of Netzach with Malkuth (pdf p103).

thoth-sun.name: Atu XIX · The Sun
thoth-sun.oneLine: Crowley's Sun: the Sun charged with a rose, Heru-ra-ha the Lord of the New Aeon.
body: Crowley says the card represents, in heraldic language, the Sun, charged with a rose, and that it represents Heru-ra-ha, the Lord of the New Aeon (pdf p105). He says the rose represents the flowering of the solar influence (pdf p105).

thoth-aeon.name: Atu XX · The Aeon
thoth-aeon.oneLine: Crowley's Aeon, once the Angel: the letter Shin for Fire, the child Horus born.
body: Crowley says the old card was called The Angel, or The Last Judgment, and that the letter Shin refers to Fire (pdf p107). He says the child Horus is born as a result of the marriage of two figures (pdf p107), and that the letter Shin appears at the bottom of the card in a form suggestive of a flower (pdf p108).

thoth-universe.name: Atu XXI · The Universe
thoth-universe.oneLine: Crowley's Universe: the letter Tau, Saturn, the Great Work accomplished.
body: Crowley says the letter Tau is attributed to Saturn, the outermost and slowest of the seven sacred planets, and that the element of earth was thrust upon the symbol (pdf p109). He says the Universe is the Celebration of the Great Work accomplished (pdf p110), and that the Universe is the manifestation of the Fool, its purpose accomplished, ready to return (pdf p110).

thoth-ace-of-wands.name: Ace of Wands
thoth-ace-of-wands.oneLine: The Root of the Powers of Fire; it pertains to Kether (Crowley).
aliases: Root of the Powers of Fire
Root of the Forces of Fire

thoth-two-of-wands.name: Two of Wands
thoth-two-of-wands.oneLine: Dominion: Mars in Aries, the Two at Chokmah

thoth-three-of-wands.name: Three of Wands
thoth-three-of-wands.oneLine: Virtue: the Sun in Aries, the Three at Binah

thoth-four-of-wands.name: Four of Wands
thoth-four-of-wands.oneLine: Completion: Venus in Aries, the Four at Chesed

thoth-five-of-wands.name: Five of Wands
thoth-five-of-wands.oneLine: Strife: Saturn and Leo, the Five at Geburah

thoth-ace-of-cups.name: Ace of Cups
thoth-ace-of-cups.oneLine: The Root of the Powers of Water; feminine complement of the Ace of Wands (Crowley).
aliases: Root of the Powers of Water

thoth-two-of-cups.name: Two of Cups
thoth-two-of-cups.oneLine: Love: Venus in Cancer, the Two at Chokmah

thoth-three-of-cups.name: Three of Cups
thoth-three-of-cups.oneLine: Abundance: Mercury in Cancer, the Three at Binah

thoth-four-of-cups.name: Four of Cups
thoth-four-of-cups.oneLine: Luxury: the Moon in Cancer, the Four at Chesed

thoth-five-of-cups.name: Five of Cups
thoth-five-of-cups.oneLine: Disappointment: Mars in Scorpio, the Five at Geburah

thoth-ace-of-swords.name: Ace of Swords
thoth-ace-of-swords.oneLine: The Root of the Powers of Air; the primordial Energy of Air (Crowley).
aliases: Root of the Powers of Air

thoth-two-of-swords.name: Two of Swords
thoth-two-of-swords.oneLine: Peace: the Moon in Libra, the Two at Chokmah

thoth-three-of-swords.name: Three of Swords
thoth-three-of-swords.oneLine: Sorrow: Saturn in Libra, the Three at Binah

thoth-four-of-swords.name: Four of Swords
thoth-four-of-swords.oneLine: Truce: Jupiter in Libra, the Four at Chesed

thoth-five-of-swords.name: Five of Swords
thoth-five-of-swords.oneLine: Defeat: Venus in Aquarius, the Five at Geburah

thoth-ace-of-disks.name: Ace of Disks
thoth-ace-of-disks.oneLine: The Root of the Powers of Earth; the entry of the Energy called Earth (Crowley).
aliases: Root of the Powers of Earth

thoth-two-of-disks.name: Two of Disks
thoth-two-of-disks.oneLine: Change: Jupiter and Capricornus, the Two at Chokmah

thoth-three-of-disks.name: Three of Disks
thoth-three-of-disks.oneLine: Work: Mars in Capricornus, the Three at Binah

thoth-four-of-disks.name: Four of Disks
thoth-four-of-disks.oneLine: Power: the Sun in Capricornus, the Four at Chesed

thoth-five-of-disks.name: Five of Disks
thoth-five-of-disks.oneLine: Worry: Mercury in Taurus, the Five at Geburah

thoth-six-of-wands.name: Six of Wands
thoth-six-of-wands.oneLine: Victory: Jupiter in Leo, the Six at Tiphareth

thoth-six-of-cups.name: Six of Cups
thoth-six-of-cups.oneLine: Pleasure: Scorpio and the Sun, the Six at Tiphareth

thoth-six-of-swords.name: Six of Swords
thoth-six-of-swords.oneLine: Science: Mercury in Aquarius, the Six at Tiphareth

thoth-six-of-disks.name: Six of Disks
thoth-six-of-disks.oneLine: Success: the Moon in Taurus, the Six at Tiphareth

thoth-seven-of-wands.name: Seven of Wands
thoth-seven-of-wands.oneLine: Valour: Mars in Leo, the Seven at Netzach

thoth-seven-of-cups.name: Seven of Cups
thoth-seven-of-cups.oneLine: Debauch: Venus in Scorpio, the Seven at Netzach

thoth-seven-of-swords.name: Seven of Swords
thoth-seven-of-swords.oneLine: Futility: the Moon in Aquarius, the Seven at Netzach

thoth-seven-of-disks.name: Seven of Disks
thoth-seven-of-disks.oneLine: Failure: Saturn in Taurus, the Seven at Netzach

decan-aries-1.name: Aries · first decan
decan-aries-1.oneLine: Aries, first decan: Mars; Crowley's Two of Wands (Dominion).
body: Crowley's card chapter for the Two of Wands names Mars in Aries (pdf p185); his text on the Wands attributes the card to the first decan of Aries (pdf p35).

albedo.oneLine: The whitening: the silver or moon condition (CW12 ¶334).
body: Jung writes that the albedo is the daybreak, and that not until the rubedo is it sunrise (CW12 ¶334). He writes that from the darkness of the unconscious comes the light of illumination, the albedo (CW14 ¶220).
